raceControls.proof: Two independent real PoolClients call canonical public enqueue/retention RPCs. Assert first PID occurs in pg_blocking_pids(second PID) before releasing the first transaction. Enqueue-first leaves one job and refuses erase; retention-first makes waiting enqueue return zero and leaves no orphan.
raceControls.basis: Four named cases PASS entails these source assertions completed; raw PID values are not emitted in logs.

raceControls.caseName: actual retention DML is atomic, bounded, clock-correct and fails closed on missing lifecycle/graph/guard facts
raceControls.proof: Independent executor backends both observed blocked behind a separately held authority-fixture row lock; after release exactly one erases and one returns request_missing.
raceControls.basis: Case PASS plus frozen source assertions. Authority is explicitly fixture-only.

evidenceSources.fallback: Authenticated gh read-only API used because plugin normalized run/commit responses omit raw head, tree and parent fields.

limitations: Source qualification on a PR merge checkout; not proof of deployed staging/production behavior.
Erasure uses synthetic historical request/policy fixtures and fixture-only authority, prepare, guard and suppression implementations.
No canonical production authority/prepare/suppression implementation or finite replay-tombstone policy is qualified by these cases.
Canonical enqueue SQL and locking candidate are exercised; no notification worker or provider sends run.
No managed database apply, customer purge, scheduler activation, provider/mail activation, browser check or deployment performed.
Unknown optional-context/referral/AE dependency graphs remain blocked until independently reviewed integration.
All 83 skips are outside the retention PG and adapter files; six whole-file skips plus one skipped case in a passing file reconcile the summary.
No raw logs, credentials, customer payloads, contact values or ephemeral authentication values are retained in this artifact.
